mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL year-over-year growth exceeding 3.0% signals persistent inflation requiring aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY growth > 3.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in UNRATE and rise in PAYEMS indicates labor market strength boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint movement of UNRATE↓ and PAYEMS↑ fails to produce positive 20-day returns in >60% of cases, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%), a FEDFUNDS increase above 2.0% triggers negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days as tightening expectations dominate market pricing.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive in >60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS > 2.0%, or regime-specific Rank IC < 0.03.
